title: UniPELT components as factorized Mirror axes
hypothesis: Factorized Mirror codes over LoRA, prefix, and adapter components will match a learned UniPELT gate composition on held-out task/layer/position combinations with fewer actual bytes, while each axis remains causally useful under ablation.
physical_object: shared base plus three component basis functions corresponding to LoRA, prefix, and adapter mechanisms
mirror_coordinate: per-component product code from task, layer, and position scalar factors
logical_multiplicity: composite PEFT adaptations across task/layer/position combinations
controls: ordinary CP factorization of each gate axis

task.teacher: sum of component functions weighted by rank-one task x layer x position gates

development.selection: fixed update budget; no fresh tuning

success_gate: Every fresh world: Mirror held-out NRMSE <=1.10x UniPELT and N36 payload <=70% UniPELT; ablation of each factor axis increases error by at least 10%.
failure_gate: Mirror misses quality/byte gate, CP control matches it exactly, or any proposed axis is causally inactive under ablation.
boundaries: Synthetic component mixture only; no PEFT fine-tuning of a pretrained Transformer.
All three component basis functions are explicitly paid.
Report generic CP equivalence and component ablations before claiming Mirror-specific value.
